-250.title: Behind the Walls
-250.description: A child grows up inside a fortified Iberian hilltop town, surrounded by farmers, craftsmen and walls built to protect the community.

-250.title: The Market at Emporion
-250.description: At the coast, Iberians encounter a wider Mediterranean world through Greek ships, pottery, wine, metals and grain.

-250.title: The Falcata
-250.description: As an adult, he joins the warriors whose speed, curved swords and small shields made Iberian fighters famous.

-250.title: At the Gate
-250.description: The walls were more than scenery: they shaped a community that lived with the possibility of conflict.

-250.title: The Offering
-250.description: Years later, he leaves a small bronze figure at a sanctuary—a human life transformed into an object that can survive for millennia.

-218.title: Under Roman Rule
-218.description: For centuries, Rome transformed Hispania through cities, roads, law and infrastructure, leaving foundations that would shape Spain long after the empire disappeared.

418.title: After Rome
418.description: As Roman authority disappeared, the Visigoths took control of much of the peninsula and built a new kingdom over the remains of the Roman world.

711.title: Córdoba at Its Height
711.description: Al-Andalus became one of medieval Europe's great centers of urban life, scholarship and exchange, bringing Islamic, Jewish and Christian cultures into close contact.

722.title: Two Frontiers
722.description: For centuries, Christian kingdoms expanded southward while Muslim states defended their territories, reshaping the political map of the peninsula until Granada fell in 1492.

1500.title: An Empire Across Oceans
1500.description: During the 16th and 17th centuries, Spain became a global power, enriched by its overseas empire while art, politics, religion and war transformed life at home.

1700.title: A Kingdom Under Pressure
1700.description: Spain entered an era of dynastic change, foreign invasion and political upheaval as its global empire weakened and much of Spanish America broke away.

1936.title: Spain Divided
1936.description: The Civil War tore Spain apart between 1936 and 1939. Nationalist victory brought Francisco Franco to power, beginning a dictatorship that lasted until 1975.

1975.title: A Country Opens
1975.description: After 1975, Spain transformed into a parliamentary democracy, joined the European Community in 1986 and emerged as a modern European society.
